Routed to `implementer` once as instructed, then verified its work independently. The fix is correct and the acceptance criteria are met.

**Final content of `src/slugify.mjs`** (the only file touched):

```js
export function slugify(input) {
  return String(input)
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
}
```

The old implementation only replaced `\s+`, so punctuation survived and edge hyphens were never trimmed; the new regex collapses each run of non-alphanumerics into a single hyphen and then strips edge hyphens.

**Evidence I observed myself** (not just the child's report):

- My own `node` assertions from the workspace root passed all required cases: `'Hello, World!'` → `'hello-world'`, `'  A  B  '` → `'a-b'`, `'C++ & Rust'` → `'c-rust'`.
- Additional checks I ran passed: `'!!!'` → `''` (no throw), `''` → `''`, `'a--b__c'` → `'a-b-c'`, `'---'` → `''`, `'123 Test!!'` → `'123-test'`, and no result contained a leading, trailing, or doubled h
